text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Friday.
- Following a sharp increase in the number of registered war invalids over the past six months of peace, the invalidity of some 20,000 war invalids to be reassessed.
- Croatian Bank for Reconstruction and Development (HBOR) and Kreditanstalt fur wiederaufbau (KfW) agree on a 30 million German marks loan aimed at kick-starting small businesses.
- If an upcoming meeting of interior ministers ends in success, Croats and Italians will no longer need passports to cross each others borders.
- A NATO official claims that Croatia will become part of NATO's partnership for peace programme only when SFOR leaves Bosnia and Herzegovina.
- Moving into a vacated Knin flat with possible prospects of keeping it costs 300 German marks on the black market.

- A social security agreement on the basis of reciprocity has been signed between Croatia and Austria, regulating social security rights of citizens when on territory of the other country. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
